reason: E1 reports the 12-electron ethanol oxidation on IrOsPtPdRhRu, supporting the first premise. E2 states that ligand and distortion effects in HEAs modify electronic properties and improve catalytic performance, supporting premises 2 and 3. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that controlled thermal treatment can adjust strain without segregation, nor do they demonstrate a direct link between d-band center shifts and ethanol oxidation selectivity in this system; E1 even cautions that d-band theory may not describe HEA activity. Thus, several key premises lack direct support.
premises: Multicomponent solid-solution catalysts can promote a 12-electron ethanol oxidation pathway
Lattice distortion in HEAs can be leveraged to tune catalytic properties
Ligand and strain effects in HEAs modify the d-band electronic structure of active sites
Shifts in the d-band center correlate with changes in adsorption energies of intermediates
Controlled post-synthesis thermal treatment can adjust lattice strain without phase segregation
